questions.name: Reports
questions.text: A bookkeeper needs to find a specific financial report in QuickBooks Online and wants to access the central location where all reports are organized. Starting from the left navigation bar, which tab opens the Report Center?

answers.text: Accounting
Reports
Dashboard
Sales

explanations.a: The Accounting tab in the left navigation bar opens the Chart of Accounts and journal entries, not the Report Center.
explanations.b: The Reports tab in the left navigation bar opens the Report Center, which organizes all available standard, custom, and management reports.
explanations.c: The Dashboard tab returns the user to the home screen, not the Report Center.
explanations.d: The Sales tab opens the Sales Center with customer and invoice views, not the Report Center.

questions.name: Reports
questions.text: A small business owner wants to quickly run a Profit and Loss report in QuickBooks Online to see income and expenses for the current month. They open the Report Center and scan the category groups. Under which Report Center group is the Profit and Loss report found?

answers.text: Who Owes You
What You Owe
For My Accountant
Business Overview

explanations.a: Who Owes You contains accounts receivable reports such as AR Aging and the Invoice List, not the Profit and Loss.
explanations.b: What You Owe contains accounts payable reports such as Unpaid Bills and AP Aging, not the Profit and Loss.
explanations.c: For My Accountant contains reports such as the Trial Balance and General Ledger, not the primary Profit and Loss.
explanations.d: The Student Guide lists the Profit and Loss report under the Business Overview group in the QBO Report Center.

questions.name: Reports
questions.objective: 8.3 Saving a report as a Favorite
questions.text: A controller frequently runs the same four reports each week and wants them accessible at the top of the Report Center without scrolling through categories. The QBO Report Center provides a quick way to mark reports for easy retrieval. How does a user mark a report as a favorite in the QBO Report Center?

answers.text: By right-clicking the report name and selecting Add to Favorites
By opening the report and clicking the star icon in the report toolbar
By clicking the green star next to the report name in the Report Center
By saving a customized version of the report with a custom name

explanations.a: Right-clicking is not the described method; the Student Guide specifies clicking the green star next to the report name.
explanations.b: The star that marks favorites is in the Report Center listing, not inside an open report's toolbar.
explanations.c: The Student Guide states that clicking the green star next to a report name in the Report Center marks it as a favorite for quick access.
explanations.d: Saving a customized report sends it to the Custom tab, but it does not automatically appear in Favorites; a star click is required.

questions.name: Reports
questions.objective: 8.3 Report tabs in the Report Center
questions.text: Upon opening the Report Center in QuickBooks Online, users see multiple tabs at the top that organize reports by purpose. A new bookkeeper wants to understand how the Report Center is organized. Which tabs are found at the top of the QBO Report Center?

answers.text: Income, Expenses, Banking, and Payroll
Standard, Custom Reports, and Management Reports
Favorites, Recent, All Reports, and Archived
Overview, Details, Summary, and Custom

explanations.a: Income, Expenses, Banking, and Payroll describe report category groups, not the top-level tabs of the Report Center.
explanations.b: The Student Guide states the Report Center has three tabs: Standard (built-in reports), Custom Reports (saved customizations), and Management Reports.
explanations.c: Favorites, Recent, All Reports, and Archived are not the tab labels described in the Student Guide for the QBO Report Center.
explanations.d: Overview, Details, Summary, and Custom are not the tab names at the top of the QBO Report Center.

questions.name: Reports
questions.text: A controller runs the Profit and Loss report and sees only category-level totals but no individual transactions. A colleague mentions they prefer to see every underlying transaction. The QBO Report Center offers a distinct report format that shows transaction-level data. What is the key difference between a Summary report and a Detail report in QBO?

answers.text: Summary reports display data by calendar year only; Detail reports can show any custom date range
Summary reports are only available in Plus and Advanced; Detail reports are available in all subscriptions
Summary reports can be exported to Excel; Detail reports can only be printed or saved as PDFs
Summary reports show totals by category without individual transactions; Detail reports list each underlying transaction

explanations.a: Both Summary and Detail reports support custom date ranges in QBO; the difference is in the level of data displayed.
explanations.b: Report types are available at all subscription levels; the type of report is not gated by subscription tier.
explanations.c: Both Summary and Detail reports can be exported to PDF and Excel; the export format is not what distinguishes them.
explanations.d: The Student Guide defines Summary reports as showing totals grouped by category, while Detail reports list every individual transaction making up those totals.

questions.name: Reports
questions.keyword: Statement of Cash Flows report group
questions.text: A lender asks a small business owner to provide a Statement of Cash Flows as part of a loan application review. The owner logs into QBO and navigates to the Report Center to find this report. Under which Report Center group is the Statement of Cash Flows found?

answers.text: For My Accountant section
Sales and Customers section
Business Overview section
What You Owe section

explanations.a: For My Accountant section contains accounting-specific reports like the Trial Balance and General Ledger, not the Statement of Cash Flows.
explanations.b: Sales and Customers section contains sales transaction reports; the Statement of Cash Flows is a financial statement, not a sales report.
explanations.c: The Student Guide lists the Statement of Cash Flows under the Business Overview section group alongside the Profit and Loss and Balance Sheet.
explanations.d: What You Owe section contains accounts payable aging reports; the Statement of Cash Flows is not an AP report.

questions.name: Reports
questions.text: A business owner opens the Profit and Loss report in QBO and wants to change the reporting period to the prior fiscal year and switch the display from accrual to cash basis. These changes are made using a toolbar that appears at the top of the open report. Which toolbar or button is used to customize an open QBO report?

answers.text: The Edit button, which opens a report properties dialog
The Customize button located above the report data
The gear icon in the upper right corner of the main screen
The Filters panel accessible from Account and Settings

explanations.a: There is no Edit button for reports; the Student Guide describes using the Customize button to modify report parameters.
explanations.b: The Student Guide states that the Customize button located above the report data allows users to change date ranges, accounting methods, columns, and filters.
explanations.c: The main gear icon manages company settings and lists, not report-level customizations.
explanations.d: Account and Settings sets company-wide defaults; individual report customization is done using the Customize button within the open report.

questions.name: Reports
questions.text: After customizing a report in QBO, a controller wants to share it with a colleague who uses Excel and also send a PDF version to the company's board of directors. The controller looks for export options within the open report. To which formats can a QBO report be exported directly from within the report?

answers.text: PDF and Excel (.xlsx)
CSV and Word (.docx)
Excel (.xlsx) and Google Sheets
PDF and QuickBooks Desktop file (.qbb)

explanations.a: The Student Guide states that QBO reports can be exported to PDF or to Excel (.xlsx) directly from the report screen.
explanations.b: CSV and Word (.docx) are not the export formats listed in the Student Guide for QBO reports.
explanations.c: Google Sheets is not a direct export target from QBO reports; the available formats are PDF and Excel.
explanations.d: QuickBooks Desktop backup files (.qbb) are not a report export format; reports export to PDF or Excel.

questions.name: Reports
questions.text: A CFO wants a Profit and Loss report emailed to them automatically every Monday morning without having to manually run or send it each week. QBO provides a feature to automate recurring report delivery. What QBO feature allows a customized report to be delivered automatically by email on a recurring schedule?

answers.text: Report automation through the Advanced section of Account and Settings
Scheduled email, configured within the Management Reports tab
Set email schedule, configured within a saved custom report in the Custom Reports tab
Recurring transactions, by creating a recurring email transaction type

explanations.a: Account and Settings > Advanced contains automation for transactions, not scheduled report emails.
explanations.b: Management Reports is a tab for narrative report packages, not the location where individual report email schedules are set.
explanations.c: The Student Guide describes using the Set email schedule option within a saved report in the Custom Reports tab to automate recurring report delivery.
explanations.d: Recurring Transactions is used to automate financial transaction entry; it does not schedule the email delivery of reports.

questions.name: Reports
questions.text: An accountant explains to a business owner how the Balance Sheet differs from the Profit and Loss in terms of the time period it covers. Unlike the P&L, which covers a date range, the Balance Sheet is structured differently. How does the date structure of a Balance Sheet differ from that of a Profit and Loss report?

answers.text: The Balance Sheet covers a full calendar year and cannot be run for custom date ranges like the Profit and Loss
Both the Balance Sheet and the Profit and Loss cover the same date range and have the same date structure
The Balance Sheet covers a date range of transactions just like the Profit and Loss report
The Balance Sheet shows financial position as of a single point in time, while the Profit and Loss covers a date range of activity

explanations.a: The Balance Sheet can be run as of any date; the key distinction is that it is an 'as of' single-date report, not that it is restricted to calendar years.
explanations.b: The two reports have different date structures; the Balance Sheet is 'as of' a date and the P&L covers a date range.
explanations.c: The Balance Sheet does not cover a date range of transactions; it shows cumulative account balances as of a specific point in time.
explanations.d: The Balance Sheet shows the company's financial position — assets, liabilities, and equity — as of a specific point in time, while the Profit and Loss covers income and expenses over a date range.

questions.name: Reports
questions.text: During a QBO training session, a participant asks how many named report groups exist within the Standard tab of the Report Center. The trainer explains that QBO organizes its standard reports into multiple distinct groups. Which set correctly lists report groups found in the Standard tab of the QBO Report Center?

answers.text: Business Overview, Who Owes You, What You Owe, Sales and Customers, Expenses and Vendors, Employees, and For My Accountant
Profit and Loss, Balance Sheet, Banking, Payroll, Inventory, and Taxes
Income Reports, Expense Reports, Payroll Reports, Tax Reports, and Audit Reports
Customer Reports, Vendor Reports, Employee Reports, and Management Reports

explanations.a: The Student Guide lists these groups in the Standard tab: Business Overview, Who Owes You, What You Owe, Sales and Customers, Expenses and Vendors, Employees, and For My Accountant (plus Sales Tax and Payroll).
explanations.b: These are report names, not the group category labels used in the Standard tab of the Report Center.
explanations.c: Income Reports, Expense Reports, and similar labels are not the group names used in the QBO Report Center's Standard tab.
explanations.d: Customer Reports and Vendor Reports are not the group labels; QBO uses Who Owes You and What You Owe along with other named groups.

questions.name: Reports
questions.text: A business owner wants to run a report that shows customer contact information alongside their outstanding balances so the billing department can follow up on overdue accounts without switching screens. They look for this report in the Report Center. Under which Report Center group is the Collections report found?

answers.text: Sales and Customers group
Expenses and Vendors
For My Accountant group
Who Owes You group

explanations.a: Sales and Customers group contains sales activity reports; the Collections report is specifically in the Who Owes You group because it focuses on overdue receivables.
explanations.b: Expenses and Vendors contains vendor transaction reports; the Collections report is about customer balances, not vendor expenses.
explanations.c: For My Accountant group contains accounting-specific reports such as the Trial Balance; the Collections report is a customer-facing AR tool.
explanations.d: The Student Guide lists the Collections report under the Who Owes You group, alongside the AR Aging Summary, Statement List, and Invoice List.

questions.name: Reports
questions.text: A QBO trainer explains that QuickBooks Online reports can be categorized into four fundamental types based on how they present data. Understanding report types helps users select the right report for the information needed. Which set correctly identifies the four report types in QBO?

answers.text: Summary, Detail, List, and Specialized
Income, Expense, Balance Sheet, and Cash Flow
Standard, Custom, Management, and Scheduled
Summary, Detail, Comparison, and Trend

explanations.a: The Student Guide identifies four QBO report types: Summary (totals by category), Detail (individual transactions), List (list data), and Specialized (unique formats like the Business Snapshot).
explanations.b: Income, Expense, Balance Sheet, and Cash Flow are financial statement categories, not report type classifications.
explanations.c: Standard, Custom, Management, and Scheduled are Report Center tab names and delivery features, not the four report type classifications.
explanations.d: Comparison and Trend are report customization options (column choices), not fundamental report type categories described in the Student Guide.

questions.name: Reports
questions.text: A controller reviewing the Profit and Loss Summary report notices that the total for Advertising Expenses seems unusually high. They want to see every individual transaction that makes up that total without leaving the report environment. QBO provides a quick way to investigate totals in summary reports. How can a user in QBO see the individual transactions behind a total displayed on a summary report?

answers.text: Export the report to Excel and use filters to isolate the relevant rows
Switch the report type from Summary to Detail using the Customize toolbar and re-run the report
Click the hyperlinked amount on the summary report to drill down to the underlying transactions
Open a separate Transaction List report and manually filter by account and date range

explanations.a: Exporting to Excel is possible but is not the built-in QBO drill-down method; it requires extra steps outside the software.
explanations.b: Switching to a Detail report re-runs the entire report and is not the interactive drill-down the Student Guide describes.
explanations.c: The Student Guide describes clicking the hyperlinked (blue underlined) amount on a summary report to drill down to the underlying detail transactions.
explanations.d: Running a separate Transaction List report is a workaround; QBO's built-in method is to click the hyperlinked amount directly in the report.
